added_lines: bereavement mass those who died in our parish during the year and their families will be remembered at masses in our parish on the weekend of the 14/15th of november. ballyconnell: saturday the 14th at 7.30, kilquiggan sunday 15th at 9.00 & clonmore sunday the 15th at 10.30. a family member will be invited to light a candle in their memory. also, there are parishioners who have lost loved ones, parent or siblings and also natives of our parish, whose funerals were celebrated elsewhere, if you would like them to be remembered by name at our bereavement mass, please give the details to our parish office by calling or by email. thought for the week failure is success in progress. have a wonderful week clonmore

following the 2024 launch of the church’s child safeguarding policy, ailish higgins, our diocesan director of safeguarding met with young people from the diocese to ask them “what does a safe & welcoming church mean to you?” thanks to all the children and young people who took part in these sessions and were open and honest about their experience of parish life.
thanks too to their parents, the group leaders and parish priests who supported the facilitation of these groups.

national board for safeguarding children in the catholic church in ireland – biannual conference the held their biannual conference from 3rd – 5th september 2025 titled: towards a restorative and transitional justice model of engaging with victims and survivors in the catholic church in ireland.
the event aimed to enhance the understanding we all have of how we must engage in a just and restorative way with those who have suffered harm in the catholic church in ireland.
our diocesan director of safeguarding and dlp attended the event and shared valuable feedback with our diocesan safeguarding committee.
the learning from the conference will help guide our practice going forward.
special thanks to the national board for organising and hosting the event.
